title: Jeff Gillette
wikitext:
{{Short description|Contemporary American artist (born 1959)}}
'''Jeff Gillette''' (born 1959) is a contemporary American artist based in [[Southern California]]. His work is known for combining consumer images with dystopian themes. His "slumscape" paintings were featured in [[Banksy|Banksy’s]] 2015 [[Dismaland]] installation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/jeff-gillettes-subversive-paintings-inspired-banksys-dismaland/|title=Meet the 'Slumscape' Painter Who Inspired Banksy's Dystopian Theme Park|last=Holmes|first=Kevin|date=2016-06-28|website=Vice|language=en|access-date=2019-09-06}}</ref>

== Influences ==

Gillette was born in 1959 and grew up in the suburbs of [[Detroit]], [[Michigan]]. He cited the TV show "[[The Wonderful World of Disney]]" as an early source of creative inspiration. During a 1978 visit to [[Disneyland]], he reportedly found the park's atmosphere unconvincing and left after 30-minutes. As an artist, he remained interested in Disney characters, especially [[Mickey Mouse]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Jeff Gillette, Moleskine Mickey, 2022 |url=https://www.harmanprojects.com/exhibitions/72/works/artworks-11833-jeff-gillette-moleskine-mickey-2022/ |website=Harman Projects |language=en}}</ref>

Gillette dropped out of college in 1982 and traveled widely, visiting locations including the [[Himalayas]] and [[Kolkata|Calcutta]], [[India]] (present-day [[Kolkata]]).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://rhodescontemporaryart.com/news/artist-interview-with-jeff-gillette-on-post-dismal|title=Artist Interview With Jeff Gillette On 'Post Dismal'|website=Rhodes Contemporary Art|language=en|access-date=2019-09-06}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> He later became a volunteer with the [[Peace Corps]]. Many of the "slumscapes" he paints are directly inspired by the residential slums he witnessed in his travels.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/arts/la-et-cm-jeff-gillette-20170530-htmlstory.html|title=Is it art, or is it trash? Jeff Gillette wants you to stomp through his 'art landfill'|date=2017-05-30|website=Los Angeles Times|language=en-US|access-date=2019-09-06}}</ref>

After moving for a teaching position in [[Orange County, California|Orange County]], [[California]] (where Disneyland is based), he began painting works that combined imagery of residential slums with [[Disney]] characters.

Gillette has cited German philosopher [[Arthur Schopenhauer]] as an influence. He has described his work as "taking the things people love and imposing the worst-case scenario [on them]".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/art/artists/jeff-gillette-in-the-studio/|title=Jeff Gillette: in the studio|last=Hawksley|first=Rupert|date=2016-06-27|work=The Telegraph|access-date=2019-09-07|language=en-GB|issn=0307-1235}}</ref>

== Exhibitions ==
Gillette has exhibited his work since 1997, with his first solo show at Broadway Gallery in [[Santa Ana, California|Santa Ana]], [[California]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.widewalls.ch/exhibition/jeff-gillette|title=Jeff Gillette|website=Widewalls|access-date=2019-09-07}}</ref>

The style for which he is currently known emerged in a solo show called "Slumscapes – Blasphemy Blowout", which depicted American fast-food restaurants such as [[McDonald's]] against backdrops of slums and well-known cartoon figures juxtaposed with religious [[iconography]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.artnet.com/Magazine/reviews/duncan/duncan12-28-99.asp|title=artnet.com Magazine Reviews - artnet.com Magazine Reviews - L.A. Confidential|website=www.artnet.com|access-date=2019-09-07}}</ref>

In 2010, Gillette held a solo show at Copro Gallery in [[Santa Monica, California|Santa Monica]] titled "Dismayland," which attracted the attention of British artist [[Banksy]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kcet.org/shows/artbound/before-banksy-painter-jeff-gillettes-dismayland-took-on-disney|title=Before Banksy, Painter Jeff Gillette's 'Dismayland' Took on Disney|last=Goldner|first=Liz|date=2015-12-13|website=KCET|language=en|access-date=2019-09-07}}</ref> The exhibition marked the beginning of the style for which he later became recognized.

In 2017, he mounted a solo show at Gregorio Escalante Gallery in [[Los Angeles]] called "Total Dismay", which turned the exhibition space into an "art landfill".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/disney-inspired-dystopian-art-landfill-features-mickey-mouse-a-trash-dump-1006572|title=Disney-Inspired Dystopian "Art Landfill" Features Mickey Mouse in a Trash Dump|website=The Hollywood Reporter|date=25 May 2017 |language=en|access-date=2019-09-07}}</ref> In the show, he premiered a series of new paintings mounted on walls and priced for thousands of dollars, while the floor was littered with paper prints that patrons would walk on top of and which were on sale for $5.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.laweekly.com/dismaland-artist-jeff-gillette-is-turning-a-chinatown-gallery-into-a-landfill/|title="Dismaland" Artist Jeff Gillette Is Turning a Chinatown Gallery Into a Landfill|last=Ohanesian|first=Liz|date=2017-05-26|website=LA Weekly|language=en-US|access-date=2019-09-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Vankin |first=Deborah |date=2017-05-30 |title=Is it art, or is it trash? Jeff Gillette wants you to stomp through his 'art landfill' |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/arts/la-et-cm-jeff-gillette-20170530-htmlstory.html |access-date=2019-09-07 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Dismaland ==
[[File:2015-09-20_Dismaland135.jpg|thumb|2015-09-20 Dismaland]]
In Spring 2015, Banksy contacted Gillette through his manager to purchase a “Minnie Hiroshima” painting.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Banksy {{!}} BANKSY DISMALAND X JEFF GILLETTE MINNIE HIROSHIMA 2 LTD EDT (2015) {{!}} Available for Sale {{!}} Artsy |url=https://www.artsy.net/artwork/banksy-banksy-dismaland-x-jeff-gillette-minnie-hiroshima-2-ltd-edt |access-date=2019-09-12 |website=www.artsy.net |language=en}}</ref> He then invited Gillette to participate in a group exhibition called Dismaland, a temporary art project organized by Banksy and built in the resort town of [[Weston-super-Mare]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/artanddesign/2015/aug/18/banksy-weston-super-mare-dismaland|title=Banksy fans flock to Weston-super-Mare after Dismaland show rumours|last=Morris|first=Steven|date=2015-08-18|work=The Guardian|access-date=2019-09-07|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077}}</ref> 

The temporary exhibition was built as a parody of the Disneyland theme park. Described by Banksy as a "family theme park unsuitable for children." It ran from August 21 to September 27, 2015. 
[[File:Dismaland_from_Clevedon_Road.JPG|thumb|Dismaland from Clevedon Road]]
The exhibition featured 58 artists, including [[Bill Barminski]], [[Damien Hirst]], [[Jenny Holzer]], [[Peter Kennard]], and [[Ben Long (British artist)|Ben Long]]. Gillette premiered six new paintings on canvas as part of his Dismaland series. Ten new works were created by Banksy, he also funded the construction of the exhibition himself. Approximately 4,000 tickets were available for sale per day, priced at £3 each.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-bristol-33999495|title=Banksy Dismaland exhibition revealed|date=2015-08-20|access-date=2019-09-07|language=en-GB}}</ref>
